name: Retro
basis: why: limited inks as flat layers, band edges wobble 'the way imperfectly aligned screen prints do'; hist: 1970s screen printing
note: The seventies palette is the style; the misregistered flat-ink bands are the process. Grain and swoosh are garnish.

lumenary.blurb: Seventies colour: warm banded tones, a cream frame and the three-stripe swoosh.

why: Seventies colour was warm and earthy: harvest gold, burnt orange, avocado and brown. Limited inks also meant flat colour layers, so this treatment cuts the picture into a few bands, one ink each, and lets the edges between them wobble the way imperfectly aligned screen prints do. The cream border and stripes finish the sense of a printed object.
how: Pick the palette and thin it to the number of bands you asked for.
Add a tiny ordered offset to each pixel so that band edges come out slightly ragged.
Cut the brightness, with adjustable contrast, into bands and print one colour per band.
Draw the three swooping stripes and add film grain.
Cut a rounded hole from a cream rectangle for the border.
history: Screen printing became a major commercial process in the first half of the twentieth century and was taken up by artists such as Andy Warhol in the 1960s. In the 1970s it filled posters, record sleeves and packaging with earth-toned flat colour, and that palette is now shorthand for the decade.
terms: How well the separate colour layers of a print line up with each other.
Printing by pushing ink through a stencilled mesh, one colour at a time.
A way of deciding which parts of a shape are inside it, used here to cut the frame’s hole.
paragraphs: This is a 1970s screen print. A palette of six warm colours is thinned to n of them, evenly spaced, and the brightness (with adjustable contrast) is cut into n bands, one colour per band. Real screen prints never register perfectly, so before the cut a tiny ordered offset is added to each pixel. It breaks the edge between bands into a slightly ragged line instead of a ruler-straight one.
Three swooping stripes, a layer of film grain and a cream border with rounded corners finish the look. The border is a rectangle with a rounded hole cut out of it, filled with the even-odd rule.

equations.note: Ordered offset from a 4 × 4 pattern; & 3 keeps the low two bits.
c(L) is the brightness after the contrast slider.

presets.text: Avocado with four bands is the classic kitchen-wall look.
Push the grain up for a worn paper feel.
Try denim blue without the stripes for a calmer print.
